o.text: Morphologically susmaq (“to be quit”) + -dur. Cognate with Turkish susturmak (“to silence”)
A derivation from Proto-Turkic *gēb (“to chew”), compare Chuvash кавле (kavle, “to chew”). Cognate with Kazakh күйіс (küyis, “cud”).

From Proto-Common Turkic *tuzak (“snare, trap”).
Cognate with
Old Uyghur [script needed] (tuzaq, “snare, trap”);
Turkish tuzak,
Kazakh тұзақ (tuzaq),
Kyrgyz тузак (tuzak),
Southern Altai тузак (tuzak),
Uzbek tuzoq,
Bashkir тоҙаҡ (tuðaq),
Tuvan дузак (duzak),
Yakut туһах (tuhaq, “snare, trap”),
etc.
From Proto-Common Turkic *kamčï (“whip”), a derivation from *kam- (“to beat, strike down”).
From Arabic اِسْتِفْتَاح (istiftāḥ). Doublet of istiftah.
Morphologically dik (“steep, upright”) + -si + -in. Cognate with Turkish tiksinmek.
